brief: docs/plans/2026-10-25-r9700-push.md Lane 3 (+ Lane 8): close the Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 prefill gap on one R9700 (HIP gfx1201) vs radiance 1.12.0 TP2 (5210 / 6133 / 5852 tok/s at 1k / 4k / 16k); bitwise work may become default with evidence, W4A8 / numerics-changing prefill only opt-in gated on KL; draft PR, results doc, trace, LOG and tuning rows.
hypothesis: The 27B prefill is GEMM-bound (MXFP4 W4A4 dequant-to-bf16 WMMA at a third of the bf16 peak), so a cheaper exact dequant plus prefill-sized tiles would speed it up bit for bit; a W4A4 fold onto the 2x-rate fp8 WMMA would roughly double the GEMM as an opt-in; and the chunk-4096 gain (rejected before as not bitwise) could be made bitwise by running short tails as chunk 256 does.

summary: Default (bitwise): MXFP4 GEMM v2 (exact bf16 dequant from bits, prefill tile table) and, for the 27B on HIP, chunk 4096 with a new 16-row prefill tail peel that reproduces chunk 256's small passes (0 of 34 prompts / 85014 rows differ). Served 27B prefill on one R9700 980 -> 1323, 1010 -> 1437, 946 -> 1351 tok/s at 1k / 4k / 16k (+35 / +42 / +43 %), decode unchanged. Opt-in INTARSIA_HIP_MXFP4_FOLD=1 (W4A4 on the fp8 WMMA, decision mx-1) serves 2043 / 2416 / 2186; prefill KL 0.165 PASS, decode-mode 0.261 vs main 0.340.
lessons: On gfx12 the fp8 and bf16 WMMA round their 16-product sums differently, so carrying a power-of-two group scale through the fp8 matrix core is not bitwise the bf16 chain, even though every product is exact.

A W4A4 checkpoint with activation QDQ amplifies last-bit sum differences into ref-noise-sized logit changes (row KL up to 0.39 on 4 tail rows), so 'nearly bitwise' schedule changes are not small for it.

Chunk-size numerics changes came only from small-row kernels (MXFP4 GEMV <= 8 rows, split-KV attention <= 16 rows); peeling those tails makes any multiple-of-256 chunk bitwise the 256 schedule on the 27B.
With the dequant ALU removed the bitwise MXFP4 GEMM only goes 82 -> 97 TFLOP/s: its cost is the BK=32 tile pipeline, not the dequant.
